findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name the single core call site (transition_core or close_ticket) that invokes reason_refusal() and rejects, so CLI/lib/MCP all inherit the refusal rather than each surface choosing whether to honor it.
evidence: Context: 'The CLI refuses an inadmissible reason while the library silently discards it'
findings.finding: The refusal rule is exposed as a value-object method `reason_refusal()`, but a frozen value object cannot itself enforce rejection — a caller must act on it. The plan says all three surfaces 'construct it' and that `transition_core`/`close_ticket` 'read the properties', but does not name the single point that ACTS on `reason_refusal()` to reject. Today the CLI refuses while the library silently discards; if each surface independently decides whether to honor the refusal, the library/MCP could again construct the object yet ignore the refusal, re-creating the divergence the plan targets.
findings.location: Approach: 'All three surfaces construct it; txn.transition_core and close_ticket read the properties.'
scenarios: Library facade constructs TransitionRequest but never calls reason_refusal(), so an inadmissible reason is silently discarded again — the divergence returns.
MCP transition_ticket constructs the object but the surface, not the core, decides whether to reject, so the refusal can drift from the CLI's behavior.
findings.suggested_fix: State that transition_core (the shared write function reached by all three surfaces) calls reason_refusal() and raises on a non-empty result, so the refusal is enforced once at the seam rather than at each construction site.
